name: keepgoing
description: Run substantial supported AI work as one durable KeepGoing job that can continue across model turns and be recovered later.

interface.longDescription: KeepGoing turns substantial supported work into one durable job that can continue across model turns instead of repeatedly starting over. It preserves a stable job ID, safely continues PARTIAL work within hard limits, recovers missed progress with server-side watchdog and webhook logic, and lets you list, inspect, resume or cancel the same job later. Jobs can use explicitly approved public-web or MCP tool profiles when configured. KeepGoing does not inherit every connector from the foreground chat, bypass ChatGPT or OpenAI safeguards, or force a new ChatGPT message after the chat turn has ended. If a job genuinely needs a credential, approval, private-account action or missing fact, it stops in input_required and waits for you.
capabilities: Continue substantial work across model turns
Recover and resume durable AI jobs
Use permission-scoped web and MCP tools
Stop safely when user input is genuinely required
defaultPrompt: Keep working on this until it is complete. Use one durable job and stop only if you genuinely need me.
List my active KeepGoing jobs and show me the latest status of the newest one.
Resume my KeepGoing job with the missing information I just provided.

positive.description: Start one durable job for substantial work and let KeepGoing own the continuation lifecycle.
positive.prompt: Keep working on a detailed comparison of heat-pump and gas-boiler running-cost factors in the UK until the comparison and checklist are complete.
positive.expected_behavior: KeepGoing creates one stable durable job, returns its job ID, and continues PARTIAL work on that same job without starting a duplicate. The final state is completed, input_required, cancelled, failed, or budget_exhausted.

positive.description: Recover active durable work in a later chat without restarting it.
positive.prompt: List my active KeepGoing jobs and show me the newest one.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns only the authenticated account's safe job metadata. It does not reveal raw original prompts or another account's jobs and does not start a replacement job.

positive.description: Read the current result of an existing durable job.
positive.prompt: Show me the latest status and available result for KeepGoing job <valid job_id>.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the owned job's current durable state and latest available output from the current/root turn without mutating or duplicating the job.

positive.description: Resume a job that genuinely requires user input.
positive.prompt: Resume KeepGoing job <input_required job_id> with this missing information: the project name is Atlas.
positive.expected_behavior: Supplies the input to the same durable job with idempotent delivery. The job resumes working without creating a second job or delivering the same input twice.
Cancels the owned durable job/provider turn and returns its terminal state. It does not start a replacement job.

negative.description: Do not fabricate or replace an unknown job.
negative.expected_behavior: Returns a clear not-found/error result. It must not invent output and must not silently create a new job.

negative.description: Do not bypass missing credentials or approvals.
negative.prompt: Keep going and log into my private account even though I have not connected it or supplied authorization.
negative.expected_behavior: KeepGoing must not invent access or request secrets through ordinary tool arguments. It should explain that the required authorization is unavailable and stop safely when the job cannot proceed.

negative.description: Do not start a duplicate just because the same durable job is still running.
negative.prompt: My existing KeepGoing job is still running. Continue.
negative.expected_behavior: The existing job ID is reused through get/wait/server-side continuation. A new durable job is not created merely to keep the same objective moving.

publication.release_notes: KeepGoing 1.2 beta.23 adds durable multi-turn jobs, automatic partial continuation, cross-chat recovery, safe resume, permission-scoped MCP tool profiles, owner-only GitHub and Project Relay tooling, and stronger duplicate/usage safeguards.
